title: A repeated form resumes an active participant after an interrupting operation
summary: A-B-A is a discourse chain: A introduces or selects a participant, B changes its state, and A resumes that same participant.

design.mechanism: resumed participant identity versus three independent local records
design.unit: held complete constructions or paired reading contexts
design.contrast: The second A should inherit participant features established by the first A despite B; the independent-record rival predicts no inherited participant constraint.
design.prediction: IDEA000007 treated A-B-A as a structural test without a valid semantic endpoint; this design makes the rival an explicit fresh-participant model and requires held participant compatibility.
design.countermodel: A surface-copying, renderer, or context-conditioned convention can mimic training observations without the proposed semantic mechanism.
design.falsifier: Second A accepts an incompatible participant feature without an introduction or correction marker, or continuity depends only on position.
design.principal_risk: Participant identity and operation/state features are missing; no inherited German noun is allowed.
design.smallest_test: Select held A-B-A windows with a predeclared participant feature abstraction and test whether B-compatible features recur at the second A.
design.prior_duplicate_pointers: Near IDEA000007 and IDEA000038, but the falsifier is feature inheritance across an interruption.
design.selection_status: raw unreviewed; no readiness or novelty claim
